verses.text: I've seen an evil under the sun, and it weighs heavily on people.

God gives someone riches, wealth, and honor, so they have everything they could want. Yet God doesn't give them the chance to enjoy it, and a stranger enjoys it instead. That's empty, and it's a terrible sickness.
Suppose someone fathers a hundred children and lives a long, long life. If they never get their fill of anything good and don't even get a burial, I say a stillborn child is better off.
The child comes in emptiness and leaves in darkness, and darkness covers its name.
It never saw the sun or knew it, yet it has more rest than that person.
Even if someone lives a thousand years twice over and never enjoys anything good, don't they all go to the same place?
People do all their work to feed themselves, yet their appetite never gets its fill.
What advantage do the wise have over fools? What does a poor person gain by knowing how to get along among the living?
Better to see what's in front of you than let your desires wander. This too is empty, like chasing the wind.
Whatever exists was named long ago. What humans are is already known, and they can't argue their case against someone stronger than they are.
More words just make for more emptiness. What does anyone gain from that?
Who knows what's good for anyone in life, through all the days of a fleeting life that passes like a shadow? Who can tell them what will happen under the sun after they're gone?
